BLOCK 1 — TRIGGER

This Webhook stands in for 'New support ticket submitted' from your Trigger sheet.

Your helpdesk tool needs to be configured to POST each new ticket to this URL (n8n shows you the exact URL once you activate the workflow).

BLOCK 2 — DATA CONTRACT

This Code node applies every rule from your Data Contract sheet: required fields, enum checks, and the documented defaults / holds for when a rule fails.

BLOCK 4 — ACTIONS

Every HTTP Request node below is an ACTION from your Actions sheet. They're pointed at https://httpbin.org/post as a placeholder so the whole workflow runs end-to-end today. Swap the URL + add real auth once you have your Helpdesk/HR/Teams endpoints.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ action: 'auto_reply', ticket_id: $json.ticket_id, employee_id: $json.requester_employee_id, message: 'We are working on it.' }) }}

BLOCK 3 — DECISION TABLE

NOTE FOR YOUR TEAM: your Data Contract says ticket_category arrives 'auto-tagged' upstream, but Decision Table Step 1 has THIS workflow classify it with an LLM. Those two rows disagree. This branch resolves it: trust an already-valid category, otherwise call the classifier. Decide as a team which behavior you actually want and say so in your write-up -- this is exactly the kind of gap your red-team round is for.

BLOCK 6 — OBSERVABILITY

Every finished path lands here. This builds the one-row-per-run trace record from your Observability sheet, then appends it. Swap the final HTTP Request for a real Google Sheets / Airtable / Postgres node once you've picked where the trace table actually lives.

Extend this: also wire 'Outcome: Hold' and 'Outcome: Dropped' in further up into this same node -- right now only the four main outcomes are logged, per your own '3 sharp rows beat 15 vague ones' rule, that's a deliberate scope cut for you to close.
